Dear Sion Buckler

Thank you for your email of 27 June 2026, requesting information from Ordnance Survey in accordance with the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) 2000, in relation to the historical depiction of a property and surrounding land historically referred to as Ty Mawr / Great House Farm.

Having reviewed your request, in our view this does not appear to be a request for information as defined under the Freedom of Information Act (2000).  A valid request for recorded information will be treated as a request under the FOIA, unless it is a routine enquiry or for information that is dealt with as part of our routine business.

We consider your request to be for mapping information which is dealt with as part of our routine business.  As a result, rather than dealing with this as an FOI request, we have forwarded your email to our Customer Services team as we feel they will be better able to deal with your request. Our Customer Services Team will aim to respond to you within 10 working days.
In the mean-time, we do have some information about Historical mapping on our website: Historical map archives | About us | OS<https://www.ordnancesurvey.co.uk/about/historical-map-archives>.
You can call customer Services on [phone redacted], or contact them via Live Chat<https://www.ordnancesurvey.co.uk/contact-us> which is available Monday to Friday 08:00 -18:00 (except for Bank Holidays). Outside of these hours, you can use the Contact Us<https://www.ordnancesurvey.co.uk/contact-us> form or email [email redacted]<[email redacted]>.

Yours sincerely

Kim Furlong for the FOI Team

Ordnance Survey Historical Enquiries Team,

I am writing to request information regarding historical Ordnance Survey mapping and naming conventions for a specific area in Llandough, near Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan (Wales).

I am researching the historical depiction of a property and surrounding land historically referred to as Ty Mawr / Great House Farm, and I am trying to understand how its labelling and placement may have changed across Ordnance Survey map editions.

Specific mapping references
The area I am examining includes the following Ordnance Survey historical map references:
38-1-608
38-1-334

I am also comparing Ordnance Survey map editions from approximately the 1950s through to the early 1970s.

Mapping issue being investigated
From comparing available historical map editions, I have observed the following:

Earlier Ordnance Survey maps (pre-1950s / early 1950s) appear to consistently show the name Ty Mawr / Great House Farm in one field or parcel location.

In later editions (circa early 1970s), the label “Ty Mawr” appears to shift position between adjacent parcels, and the descriptor “Farm” appears to be applied or positioned differently than in earlier mapping.

There also appears to be a change in how the surrounding land parcels are labelled or visually grouped.

What I am seeking clarification on
Could you please advise:

Whether Ordnance Survey records show any map revision notes, resurvey information, or internal documentation explaining changes in naming or label placement for this area between approximately 1950 and 1975
Whether changes such as the movement of a name between adjacent parcels would typically result from:

resurvey work or updated field recording
cartographic generalisation or redraw practices
changes in naming conventions or feature classification
Whether OS holds any guidance or archival material explaining how estate names or farm names were assigned, repositioned, or reinterpreted across map editions in this period

Which historical Ordnance Survey editions or map series would best show the most accurate progression of naming and label placement for this specific site

If possible, I would also appreciate guidance on accessing any archived mapping sheets or revision history material relevant to this location.

Thank you for your assistance. I appreciate your time in helping clarify how Ordnance Survey mapping practices evolved during this period.

Kind regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergenant)

Life Member @ Royal Signals
